PullRequest.Title: agentHost: un-skip the durable workspace transition restart test with a disk I/O budget
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #339669

Un-skips `SessionWorkspaceConversionService` › `restores one durable transition before provider output after service restart`, skipped as flaky in #340007 (ff275a2dfa5), and gives it an explicit 10s budget for its on-disk SQLite I/O.

## Original failures

ADO **Flaky Smoke Tests** build [480377](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480377) (`main` @ `0817aaa8245`, Oct 4), **Linux / 🧪 Unit test iteration 11/20 (node.js)** and **13/20 (node.js)**: 2 failures in 20 iterations, both:

```
Error: Timeout of 2000ms exceeded. … (vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionWorkspaceConversion.test)
```

In the same build, iteration 10/20 failed the `SessionDatabase` sibling `snapshot persists across a database restart` with the same 2000ms timeout (#339662). Its follow-on `the latest snapshot remains pending when relay is interrupted` failure (`SessionDatabase has been disposed`) was caused by the timed-out test's `finally` closing the shared database.

## Root cause

This is not a logic race. The test opens a **real SQLite file**, writes, closes it, reopens it and reads it back. Each commit flushes to disk, and `strace -f -c -e fsync,fdatasync` in CI counted **40 `fsync` calls for two executions**, about 20 per execution. Its duration therefore depends on the disk:

- In the failing ADO build, the test took **93–120ms in its 18 passing Linux iterations** (under 75ms on macOS, where `fsync` does not flush to the device). It then went over 2000ms in the other 2. The `SessionDatabase` restart tests with the same open/close/reopen pattern behaved the same way (45–59ms, then one >2000ms timeout).
- ADO reported a 2000ms timeout here, mocha's default, while GitHub Actions node.js runs get 30000ms (`IS_CI` in `test/unit/node/index.js`). So the test only fails where a filesystem stall can use up a 2s budget.
- The `SessionDatabase` siblings with the same problem were fixed with an explicit `.timeout(10_000)` in #340024 (Fixes #339662).

## Fix

Un-skip the test with `.timeout(10_000)` and a one-line comment explaining why, matching #340024.

## Stress results

Diagnostic draft #342352 ran the test body on **Linux / Electron-Unit CI** through the node.js runner. Each iteration ran it twice, once with a 2s budget (the ADO budget, "before") and once with the 10s budget ("after"):

| Run | Disk load | Iterations per budget | 2s budget failures | 10s budget failures | Slowest iteration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [1](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39080755489/job/117537025835) | none | 1500 | 0 | 0 | 791ms |
| [1](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39080755489/job/117537025835) | 1 × `dd conv=fsync` | 1500 | 0 | 0 | 640ms (typical ~630ms) |
| [2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39081590471/job/117539612469) | none | 500 | 0 | 0 | **1189ms** |
| [2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39081590471/job/117539612469) | 4 × `dd oflag=direct conv=fsync` | 300 | 0 | 0 | 1340ms |
| [3](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39082263761/job/117541478254) | none | 500 | 0 | 0 | 139ms |
| [3](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39082263761/job/117541478254) | 4 × `dd oflag=direct conv=fsync` | 300 | 0 | 0 | **1449ms** |
| **Total** | | **4600** | **0** | **0** | |

GitHub runners did not reproduce a stall over 2s. They did show the heavy tail behind the ADO failures: a ~50ms median, quiet-disk outliers of 0.8–1.2s, and up to 1.45s under contention. That's 72% of the 2s budget, while every iteration stayed under 15% of the new 10s budget. Locally on macOS: 200 / 200 passed without load and 600 / 600 under one busy loop per core (max 580ms) with a 2000ms timeout.

## Validation

- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --timeout 2000 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionWorkspaceConversion.test.ts` (CI node.js entry point with the ADO default budget): passed, 120 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionWorkspaceConversion.test.ts`: passed, 120 passing.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionWorkspaceConversion.test.ts`: passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Node.js unit-test execution of the durable workspace-transition restart case
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test runner now waits for temporary-directory creation, the first on-disk SQLite open/migrations and writes, connection close, reopen/read, final close, and directory removal. All of this is intentionally on this single test's critical path; no production/startup/rendering path is changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and recursively remove one uniquely named temporary directory containing the SQLite file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdtemp and one rm per execution of this single test; fixed independently of repository, session, or turn count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test was skipped, so these filesystem operations did not run in normal suite execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both operations must complete before the test can finish; cleanup remains bounded to the test's unique directory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/create and migrate one on-disk SQLite database, persist one workspace conversion and associated metadata/event state, close it, reopen it, read transitions, and close it during cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two SQLite connection opens, two lifecycle closes, and a fixed workload for one transition/provider turn per test execution; no collection-driven fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The skipped test performed no SQLite I/O during normal suite execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These awaited operations dominate this test's latency and are the reason for the explicit 10-second timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test fixtures: one session, one workspace transition, and one provider turn. Cost scales only with the external number of test-suite invocations, not with user data or a changed loop within one invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The body awaits the setup, writes, first close, reopen, and read sequentially. Cleanup uses Promise.all for at most the two database handles, but on the successful path the first handle has already been closed and cleared, so only the restored handle closes. There is no per-item concurrency or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first open is cold for the newly created database and runs migrations; the reopen may benefit from the OS page cache but intentionally exercises durable state. There is no application cache, cache key, miss retry, or coalescing behavior added by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed test registration directly changes the case from skipped to executed, and the body explicitly awaits the two SQLite lifecycles and temporary filesystem cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Disk stalls can vary substantially by CI host, hence the 10-second budget, but each execution remains a single fixed-size restart test. The exact CI time increase depends on filesystem contention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Re-enabling the test intentionally adds bounded CI-only disk I/O and the timeout only expands the allowed wait; it does not add repeated work, collection-scaled fan-out, unbounded retention, or production-path latency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced the newly enabled test through its temporary filesystem and SQLite boundaries. The change adds one bounded, serial, fixed-size disk-backed test execution and an explicit timeout; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
